results.reason: Issue 5 cites § 2.2's automatic five-year renewals and the 240–270 day notice requirement. It calls this a narrow 30-day band and says missing it locks Harrowgate in through 2032.

Issue 1 quotes § 3.1 (all glass and PET containers, any beverage product, worldwide) and contrasts it with the term sheet's amber glass, beer-only, U.S./Canada scope. Issue 8 explains the integration clause binds Harrowgate to the executed text.
Issue 3 notes receipt on August 3, 2026 per Recital C. It says the 30-day window expired September 2, before the September 21 amendment, so the increase is deemed accepted.

Issue 2 explains that Amendment § 2.1 deletes the recall-cost carve-out and limits the indemnity carve-out to IP claims under § 9.1(c). It says recall and personal-injury exposure is now subject to the six-month-fees cap.

The new § 14.4 and its override of § 14.3 are identified. However, the response never says nothing prevents assignment to a competitor, and never notes that Harrowgate remains bound by the consent requirement, making the restriction one-sided.
The response never mentions § 15.2 or that written amendments take precedence over the Supply Agreement.
The response repeatedly describes the § 11.1 cap as six months of container fees, which substantively states the cap measure.
The memo is addressed to [Partner] and lists issues item by item. Each item has a 'Where' section citation and a 'Recommended fix'.
The response proposes specific language, including a restored § 11.2, a narrowed § 3.1, and a revised § 14.4.
The response concludes the objection window expired and the increase is deemed accepted. It only suggests exploring whether the notice was deficient.
The response states the integration clause means the executed broader text governs and the term sheet is only evidence.
